text: grep -rn "output-buffer funnel\|goes to stdout\|puts both on stdout" docs/ | head: docs/php/streams.md:484:| `stream_wrapper_restore()` | `stream_wrapper_restore(string $protocol): bool` | Clears the disabled bit `stream_wrapper_unregister()` set on a built-in wrapper, and answers PHP's three cases. A wrapper that really was unregistered is restored silently and reports `true`. One that was never unregistered reports `true` with `Notice: stream_wrapper_restore(): <proto>:// was never changed, nothing to restore`. A scheme that never existed reports `false` with `Warning: stream_wrapper_restore(): <proto>:// never existed, nothing to restore`, which `@` suppresses. Both go to stdout through the output-buffer funnel, which is where PHP CLI puts them. |
